To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
agrin, LRP4 and MuSK are involved in the development of the dendritic tree and synapse formation of cultured mouse embryonic neurons.

(i) agrin, LRP4 and MUSK are required for dendritogenesis and for the formation of excitatory synapses in the developing CNS; (ii) agrin, but not LRP4 or MUSK, regulates inhibitory synaptogenesis; (iii) agrin, via LRP4, increases the size and density but not the number of excitatory synapse-associated puncta; (iv) agrin, independently of LRP4, regulates dend

agrin induces dendrite branching in cultured embryonic neurons, an effect mediated by Lrp4, but not MuSK, and that agrin induces an Lrp4 and a MuSK-dependent increase of excitatoric synapses and an agrin-induced decrease in inhibitory synapses in cultured embryonic cortical neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of synaptic development.
the molecular basis of synapse formation in the developing nervous system.
the development and function of synapses, the junctions between neurons and muscle cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Lrp4-MuSK complex is essential for the induction of excitatory synapses and that agrin can induce excitatory synapse formation independently of Lrp4 and the Lrp4- MuSK complex, but that agrin can also act via Lrp4 and/or the Lrp4 -MuSK complex to increase the density of excitative synapses.
agrin and Lrp4 have a role in dendritic arborisation and synapse development in cultured CNS neurons, but that the role of MuSK is not clear.
agrin and Lrp4, but not MuSK, are involved in the regulation of dendritic arborisation and synaptogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Lrp4 is necessary for dendritic arborisation and synaptogenesis whereas MuSK and agrin play only a minor role in this process in the cultured CNS neurons.
agrin is a key player in dendritic arborisation and synaptogenesis, with Lrp4 and to a lesser extent MuSK as modulators of these processes.
agrin, LRP4 and MuSK are involved in different aspects of dendritic development, and that agrin and LRP4 are involved in different steps of synaptogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the agrin-Lrp4-MuSK pathway is involved in dendritic arborisation and synaptogenesis during development of the central nervous system.
agrin is a key organizer of dendritogenesis, synaptogenesis and synapse composition.
agrin, LRP4 and MuSK have distinct roles during the development of the nervous system.
